jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
Company Description
GLOBAL AGENCY FOR COMMUNITY ACCELERATION (GACA) is a community-based organization focused on empowering young people of all genders to drive social, cultural, economic, and political development in their communities. GACA works to equip youth with knowledge, information, and practical skills so they can engage meaningfully in grassroots community development and help find sustainable solutions to local challenges. The organization prioritizes access to quality education for vulnerable children from humble backgrounds, supporting them to realize their potential and become impactful members of society. GACA also promotes talent development among young children, partners with other organizations to deliver mind education that builds self-awareness and productivity, and advocates for clean water and a healthy environment in the communities it serves.
Role Description
The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will provide strategic leadership and overall direction for GACA’s programs and partnerships as a volunteer in a remote role. This position is responsible for shaping and implementing the organization’s vision, overseeing operational and financial management, and ensuring that initiatives focused on youth empowerment, education, and community development are aligned with GACA’s mission. Day-to-day tasks include collaborating with internal teams and external partners, developing plans for program expansion, monitoring impact, and guiding resource allocation to support key projects. The CEO will also represent GACA in stakeholder engagements, support fundraising and partnership development, and foster a culture of accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement across the organization.
Qualifications

Strategic leadership skills, including Strategic Planning and Business Planning, to guide organizational growth and program development.
Operational expertise, including Operations Management, to oversee daily functions, program delivery, and organizational effectiveness.
Financial acumen, including Finance skills, to support budgeting, resource stewardship, and long-term sustainability.
Revenue and relationship-building skills, including Sales, to help expand partnerships, funding opportunities, and community engagement.
Previous experience in nonprofit or community-based organizations, especially in youth empowerment, education, or social development.
Strong communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management abilities, with capacity to lead diverse teams in a remote environment.
Demonstrated commitment to equity, inclusion, and community-driven solutions.
Relevant academic background in business, public administration, social sciences, or a related field is beneficial but not required if compensated by experience.

jobs.description:
Sustainable Ocean Alliance
Sustainable Ocean Alliance (SOA) is a global nonprofit on a mission to restore ocean health by
unleashing the power of next-generation leaders, bold innovation, and collective action. We work at the intersection of entrepreneurship, policy, and community, supporting early-stage ocean solutions and mobilizing our worldwide network to turn ideas into impact. 

2026 marked our twelfth year of growing influence and over a decade of bold action to protect ocean health and build climate resilience. 

Context and moment
SOA has been successful with foundation funding and has a team in place for this work. Now, we are looking to hire an individual with experience  independently  identifying, cultivating, and closing individual gifts.

Enter the Director of Development
The Director of Development will design a fundraising approach for individual giving, develop prospects, cultivate relationships, and close gifts. This role will report to the CEO and will play a key role in building our growth trajectory and philanthropic community. 

We are currently prioritizing cultivating relationships and closing individual gifts over developing advanced processes, systems, engagement plans, events, and infrastructure. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports, thus the focus on independently closing. 

Accountabilities
Cultivate, solicit, close, and steward six- and seven-figure gifts.
Develop and execute a multi-year fundraising strategy to grow unrestricted and restricted support (who to approach and how), with an emphasis on accelerating unrestricted funding.
Recommend strategies to approach and engage major donors and family offices.
Develop messaging for donors  and  simple and clear collateral for them.
Translate the organization’s mission and impact into attractive and honest narratives.
Build donor relationships rooted in trust, inspiration, and impact.
Be present, informed, and engaged for various small salons and dinners with donors. 
Build and manage a portfolio of prospects and donors.
Identify and pursue new donor networks and funding opportunities.
Leverage CEO and Board networks and introductions where possible.

Qualifications
Previous success  independently  identifying, cultivating, and closing six and seven figure gifts 
Previous success developing differentiated fundraising strategies (who and how)
Experience building with executive leadership and boards
Experience building the pitch and collateral
An ability to build trusted relationships
An ability to listen to donor interests and needs
An ability to make a clear and direct ask
Excellent communication skills 
An ability to collaborate with program teams to understand the work
Strong and organized execution
Interest in mission-driven work

Preferred
Experience fundraising for ocean, climate, environmental, or social impact sectors

Location and total rewards
Locations (San Francisco Bay Area or NYC). Remote flexibility. 
150,000 - 160,000 USD salary. Title is negotiable.
Strong benefit package (6% retirement match; 100% of premiums for medical insurance for employees, 50% of medical insurance premiums for dependents; 100% of dental and vision premiums; good PTO that grows with tenure; 100% of premiums on basic life and AD&D)

Apply early as applications will be reviewed and interviews scheduled on a rolling basis.

jobs.title: Development Director
jobs.description:
Since 1981, Friends of the Urban Forest, a premier San Francisco environmental nonprofit, has brought together communities throughout the city to plant more than 60,000 trees — half of San Francisco’s street tree canopy. Friends of the Urban Forest has a long history of integrating urban greening with civic engagement as a way to increase community health and resilience, combat the effects of the climate crisis, and promote environmental equity and social justice. Friends of the Urban Forest recognizes San Francisco’s many communities and cultures and the diverse ways in which they connect with our urban forest. We also connect San Franciscans to nature and to each other.

This position at Friends of the Urban Forest would give you the exciting opportunity to be part of a growing and dynamic professional organization that has been creating a greener San Francisco for over 45 years.

Position Overview

The Development Director is responsible for designing, implementing, and evaluating a comprehensive fundraising strategy that ensures the long-term sustainability and growth of Friends of the Urban Forest, generating between $1.5 and $2 million in contributed revenue annually. This includes oversight of all annual, major, and planned giving; foundation and corporate relations; events; and communications that support donor engagement. The Development Director serves as a strategic thought partner to the Executive Director and the rest of the Senior Leadership Team, working closely with the Board of Directors and staff to strengthen Friends of the Urban Forest’s culture of philanthropy.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned fundraising professional with excellent leadership skills, a collaborative spirit, and a deep commitment to environmental justice and community empowerment.

Please note this job announcement is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Planning

Develop and execute a multi-year fundraising strategy aligned with organizational goals.
Partner with the Executive Director, the rest of the Senior Leadership Team, and Board to strengthen philanthropy, cultivate donor relationships, and expand fundraising capacity.
Provide regular analysis, projections, and strategic recommendations to organizational leadership.
Grow total annual contributed revenue and specifically, unrestricted funding.
Strengthen cross-departmental collaboration with Programs, Finance and Operations.

Team Management & Culture Building

Hire, supervise, support, and mentor a small team of experienced resource development staff.
Foster a collaborative, values-driven department that centers equity, curiosity, accountability, and continuous learning.
Ensure clear roles, workflows, and performance benchmarks.

Fundraising & Donor Engagement

Lead the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of major donors and institutional funders.
Oversee proposal development, reporting, events, donor communications, and development of CRM standards and donation platforms.
Expand and diversify the donor base while strengthening engagement with long-time supporters and community partners.

Collaboration & External Relations

Work closely with program staff to understand organizational priorities and articulate compelling case statements.
Represent Friends of the Urban Forest at events, donor meetings, partner gatherings, and community forums as needed.
Collaborate with communications staff to ensure consistent, mission-aligned messaging.
Collaborate with finance staff to ensure systems accurately report and classify revenue.

Qualifications

7+ years of progressively responsible fundraising experience, preferably in environmental, community development, or social justice organizations.
Proven success in major gifts, foundation relations, and donor strategy development.
Demonstrated experience supervising and developing staff.
Exceptional communication, relationship-building, and storytelling skills.
Strong project management skills and comfort juggling multiple priorities.
Commitment to equity, inclusion, and community-centered practices.
Passion for sustainability, climate resilience, and urban forestry is strongly preferred.

Competitive Compensation and Benefits

The Development Director position is full-time, exempt with an annual salary of $130,000 - $145,000. Friends of the Urban Forest offers a competitive benefits package that includes 100% employer-paid medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, life, and AD&D insurance for employees and 50% for dependents (up to a certain limit). We offer a 403(b) Retirement Plan with an employer match, a generous paid leave policy that includes 13 holidays each year, vacation starting at 12 days and increasing with additional years of employment, 10 sick days and funds for professional development opportunities.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Friends of the Urban Forest is dedicated to gender and race equity and inclusion. As an equal opportunity employer, Friends of the Urban Forest does not discriminate against any applicant or employee on the basis of any status or characteristic protected by applicable laws or ordinances. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Flexible and Safe Work Environment

The position currently operates in a hybrid model with approximately 50% time working in the office located in the Presidio of San Francisco and 50% time working remotely.

Friends of the Urban Forest is committed to maintaining a safe and healthy environment for all employees. In an effort to avoid serious health and safety risks and significant disruption to our work, we have taken measures to protect against the spread of COVID-19 including a mandatory vaccination policy. New hires will be asked to provide proof of vaccination on the first day of employment.  

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Office workspaces are often shared and employees should not have any expectation that they can be assigned a dedicated workspace.

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

At Braille Institute, we are driven by a shared purpose: to serve the blind and low vision community. We come together to make a meaningful difference in the lives of others, finding fulfillment in the impact we create. We believe in fostering a culture that is collaborative, inclusive, and flexible.

We understand the importance of work-life balance, valuing both personal and professional fulfillment. Here, you'll find an environment that supports your well-being while providing opportunities to learn, grow, and thrive alongside colleagues who are sighted and visually impaired.

OVERVIEW:

Braille Institute’s Development team raises funds that work to eliminate barriers to a fulfilling life caused by low vision or complete sight loss. The fundraising team is comprised of 16 members who work closely on annual giving, mid-level giving, major gifts, planned gifts, capital projects, and campaigns. Founded in 1919, Braille Institute of America (BIA) is one of the oldest and most comprehensive providers of free services for people who are blind or visually impaired. BIA has an annual operating budget of approximately $30 million and is funded almost entirely through private donations.

JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Job Summary:

The Director of Development – Orange County serves as the organization’s lead fundraiser and development representative for the Orange County region (with potential support for Riverside County). This role manages a strategic portfolio of major gift pros strategy and regional implementation of the organization’s major gifts strategy and plays a central role in advancing the Together for Impact culture across the region.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

The Director of Development manages a strategic portfolio of major gift prospects in Orange County (and, as needed, Riverside) and is responsible for cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding donors capable of making gifts between $10,000 and $100,000, building a robust regional pipeline, and contributing to a team revenue goal of $5M+.

This position collaborates closely with the Senior Director of Development, regional leadership, the Director of Planned Giving, the San Diego Gift Officer, and cross‑departmental partners to advance regional fundraising priorities. The Director maintains high standards of data integrity, oversees regional dashboards and forecasting, and ensures accurate documentation of donor interactions.

As a senior representative of the organization, the Director builds community partnerships, participates in regional events, and promotes the organization’s mission to donors, prospects, volunteers, and community stakeholders.

As a director, this role must maintain knowledge of Braille Institute of America programs and services for use in meetings and solicitations. The role must also attend donor, volunteer, student and community events to promote the organization and solicit gifts, as appropriate.

Perform other duties as assigned. As the organization continues to evolve, duties or tasks may change without impacting the overall Job Description.

Supervisory Responsibilities:
None

QUALIFICATIONS:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills and/or abilities required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job duties.

Knowledge and Education:
A bachelor's degree or equivalent experience is desired. Advanced knowledge of fundraising techniques, moves management, communication strategies, including writing/editing.

Skills and Abilities:
Position requires excellent written and verbal communication skills, strategic thinking, and strong interpersonal skills. Must have proven ability to establish and maintain donor relationships and secure funds from donors.

Experience:
Five years minimum in a fundraising position or equivalent experience

Certifications/licenses:
Valid driver's license is preferred

Work Environment:
Position works in a standard office environment which may be remote. Travel in the Southern California area is required.

Physical Requirements:
Position operates standard office equipment.

Salary range: $110,000-$125,000

jobs.title: Program Director (La Central YMCA)
jobs.description:
Full-Time / Regular

$66,300 Salaried

The YMCA of Greater New York is here for all New Yorkers — to empower youth, improve health, and strengthen community. Founded in 1852, today the Y serves a diverse population of more than half a million New Yorkers who learn, grow, and thrive through programs and services at our 24 branches. Community is the cornerstone of the Y. Together, we connect active, engaged New Yorkers to build stronger communities.

To help fulfill our mission, we cultivate a culture of learning, leading, and collaboration to enhance community impact. Through our talented staff and “LEAP” career framework (Leadership, Empowerment, Accountability, Personal Growth), we are committed to a people-first approach that fosters trust, inclusion, growth, and development for all.

Being part of the YMCA Afterschool staff team is a deeply rewarding job where you support children’s learning, help build strong connections, and have a positive impact on so many in your community. At Y Afterschool, we will create a safe and fun space for kids to learn and grow, lead creative activities, and help them develop valuable skills. This is an opportunity to make a real difference and gain invaluable leadership and interpersonal experience.

The La Central YMCA is seeking a Program Director. Under the supervision of the Youth & Family Director, the Program Director serves as the strategic and operational leader for our Afterschool initiative. This multifaceted role requires a dynamic professional capable of managing all aspects of a successful, holistic youth development program.

Team Leadership: Supervising, mentoring, and leading a diverse staff team to deliver high-quality programming.
Program Excellence: Designing, creating, and implementing engaging and impactful programming that meets the developmental needs of all participants.
Inclusion and Mental Wellness: Prioritizing and integrating mental health support, case management, and social-emotional learning initiatives for both program participants and staff. Ensuring programming and day-to-day operations are welcoming to children of all abilities.
Operational Management: Meticulously managing site budgets, ensuring fiscal responsibility, and maintaining compliance with all contractual agreements and reporting requirements.

Key Responsibilities:

Direct programs serving the designated grade level band (K-5 or 6-8), ensuring all activities and services are age-appropriate and aligned with DYCD program requirements.
Ensure programs and services are deeply integrated into the specific community we serve and meet the diverse needs of all community members.
Develop and execute effective strategies for recruiting and retaining participants, aiming for consistently high attendance rates and sustained program engagement.
Develop and utilize quantitative measures, quality monitoring tools, and external evaluations to demonstrate program effectiveness.
Routinely analyze data and assessment results to identify trends, measure outcomes, and implement adjustments designed to continuously improve program quality and meet or exceed all established program goals.
Successfully establish, maintain, and leverage connections with local community partners, public/private funders, and external evaluators to enhance program services, increase resource availability, and ensure sustained program success.
Foster and lead staff in the implementation of comprehensive mental wellness support for both participants and families. Provide mental wellness resources to kids and families, and ensure staff are well-trained to create a supportive environment and identify participants who may benefit from mental wellness support/referrals.
Coordinate and implement a crisis plan to support various participant/family needs in conjunction with NYCPS school social workers, mental health staff, and external behavioral health providers.
Oversee the selection of an evidence-based SEL curriculum that is adaptable to a dynamic after-school setting (COMPASS Elementary or SONYC). Ensure all SEL programming is deliberate and clearly defines the specific social and emotional competencies that staff seek to develop in participants.
Manage the program budget, order all supplies in a timely manner, and track all expenses using the tools provided.
Recruit and retain a strong staff team with diverse abilities and backgrounds. Team skills and schedules must ensure that all aspects of the COMPASS program are delivered with an outstanding level of program quality.
Cultivate and maintain strong, collaborative working relationships with host school administration and staff.
Proactively coordinate and discuss planned activity schedules, particularly those related to STEAM and Literacy initiatives, to ensure alignment and integration with the host school's academic goals.
Maintain accurate program documentation as required by the Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS), Department of Health (DOH), Department of Youth & Community Development (DYCD), and YMCA of Greater New York.
Understand and communicate the YMCA’s core values and the goals of the Y Afterschool Program to participants and caregivers.
Develop and maintain positive relationships with parents/guardians and caregivers through regular communication regarding their child’s strengths and areas for growth. Manage communications regarding injuries or incidents, as needed.
Actively participate in training sessions, designated meetings, and special events.
Adhere to all Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS), Department of Health (DOH), YMCA of Greater New York, school partner, and funder standards, expectations, and regulations.

Desired Skills & Experience:

Must have one (1) of the following:
Associate’s Degree in Child Development, Elementary Education, Physical Education, Recreation, or a related field;
A New York State Children’s Program Administrator Credential;
A School-Age Child Care Credential or other Office-recognized credential specific to the school-age developmental period;
Two (2) years of college with 18 credits in Child Development, Elementary Education, Physical Education, Recreation, or a related field.

Minimum of two (2) years of direct experience working with children under the age of 13.
Minimum of one (1) year of experience in a supervisory capacity in a childcare program or related field of work.
Current Pediatrics CPR or First Aid certification preferred.
General knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Strong interpersonal skills, leadership qualities, and comfortable working with diverse youth and adults.

Benefits:

The YMCA of Greater New York offers a variety of benefits to its staff members, including retirement benefits , medical, paid time off, free YMCA membership, and more! Benefit eligibility is determined by an individual’s employment status (i.e., full-time or part-time), tenure, and/or the number of hours scheduled to work. Click here for more information.

How to Apply:
If you would like to be a member of our dynamic team, please complete our online application and submit your résumé and a thoughtful cover letter that explains your interest in the role and our organization.

If you are a current YMCA employee, please submit your application through the Internal Career Site in Cornerstone.

jobs.title: Director of Development & Communications
jobs.description:
About Climate Emergency Fund

Climate Emergency Fund is a critical institution in the climate movement – raising money for and making grants to nonviolent, disruptive climate groups because that is the fastest way to create transformative change. We act as a venture philanthropy providing seed funding to groups like Just Stop Oil, Climate Defiance, Scientist Rebellion, and others. We are a bridge between funders and activists, and we engage in funder education about social movements and their need for a radical flank to change what is politically possible.
Position Summary
Climate Emergency Fund’s director of development and communications (DDC) will fundraise for heroic activists who are changing the world! The DDC must be passionate about the climate movement, mass protest and nonviolent action – being mission-aligned is critical. Fundraising is the heart of what we do with all team members contributing to the work of the development team. The DDC plays a pivotal role in the management, support, and direct implementation of our fundraising goals and strategy. To that end, our communications approach happens largely through the lens of fundraising, with messaging strategies developed to engage funders and the philanthropic community around our goals. A savvy director of development and communications will be a skilled communicator as well and will work to amplify and spotlight the successes of our grantees and the impact and effectiveness of our theory of change. 
The DDC will collaborate closely with and support the executive director in growing a thriving donor portfolio, including coordinating virtual and in-person events and conferences. The DDC will identify and build new funding opportunities and oversee core processes of our fundraising and donor management, leading a team, including a development officer and a development operations manager.
Responsibilities include:
Fundraising
. Collaborate with the executive director, board of directors, and development team in cultivating and soliciting major and leadership gifts, as well as overseeing the wider development program - 45% 
Plan and execute an 18-month fundraising strategy, including virtual and in-person fundraising events and conferences or speaking opportunities.
Set specific goals and build out necessary KPIs for increasing annual organizational revenue. 
Work with the development team to build and implement a structured donor pipeline for converting, upgrading, and retaining donors through regular touchpoints and outreach.
Manage a portfolio of major and leadership donors. 
Support ED in managing a portfolio of donors.
Work with ED to support cultivation of board of directors’ networks.
Identify and research major donors, major donor prospects, and institutional grant opportunities in collaboration with the team.
Communications
. Support development and distribution of a multi-channel comms strategy - 20% 
Oversee the development and execution of overall fundraising and communications collateral, including mass emails, acknowledgment letters, LOIs, proposals, grant applications, decks, and our annual reports.
Partner with ED and external communications team in the preparation of op-eds, speaking engagements, press releases, new fundraising initiatives and collateral, and crisis communications.
Engage with comms team attending weekly meetings, reviewing media monitoring, and make appropriate recommendations to ED.
Manage fundraising content that’s shared across the website, newsletters, social media, digital ad spaces, and other platforms.
Management and Administration
. Oversee infrastructure, managing a savvy fundraising team - 35%
Manage the development and communications teams and provide leadership and support to the full team, including the program officer and operations officer, ensuring collaboration across departments. 
Oversee development team’s grant management work, including the institutional grants Asana project, and the grant tracker, including all touchpoints for outreach and engagement.

jobs.description:
Your opportunity

Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments

Overview

The Managing Director & Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments will report to the Chief Executive Officer of Schwab Asset Management and lead a team responsible for managing our expanding portfolio of non-traditional investment management offerings including the planned launch of the Schwab Private Company Fund.

Key Outcomes

This leader will be accountable for establishing the strategic direction, investment governance, operating model, and risk discipline required to scale Schwab’s private assets and alternative investments platform. The role requires sound independent judgment within approved investment guidelines, strong executive presence, and the ability to connect investment strategy, product innovation, risk management, and client outcomes across SAM/CSIM and the broader Schwab enterprise.

Set the long-term strategic agenda for Private Assets and Alternative Investments, including portfolio construction philosophy, product roadmap, governance standards, risk controls, and operating discipline across current and future offerings.
Lead the successful development, launch, and scaling of the Schwab Private Company Fund and related offerings, ensuring investment design, legal structure, compliance oversight, operations, distribution readiness, and client experience are aligned from concept through commercialization.
Make independent investment and business decisions within approved guidelines, balancing growth, liquidity, valuation, manager selection, operational complexity, fiduciary obligations, regulatory expectations, and Schwab’s reputation for client-first stewardship.
Oversee risk across the Private Assets and Alternative Investments platform, partnering closely with Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, and Technology teams to ensure strong controls, clear accountability, scalable processes, and effective issue escalation.
Serve as a senior investment and business advisor to the Chief Executive Officer of SAM/CSIM and the broader executive team, providing informed perspectives on private markets, alternative investment trends, fund performance, competitive dynamics, product opportunities, and enterprise implications.
Represent the platform with credibility before the Funds Board of Directors, SAM/CSIM committees, firm-wide risk committees, regulators, and senior enterprise stakeholders, translating complex investment, liquidity, valuation, and governance topics into clear executive-level recommendations.
Partner with leadership on the construction and oversight of SPVs serving as building blocks for the Schwab Private Company Fund, ensuring close coordination across sourcing, due diligence, structuring, valuation, operational readiness, and ongoing monitoring.
Provide leadership and expertise to third-party investment oversight and asset allocation forums involving private assets, helping shape manager due diligence, allocation recommendations, risk evaluation, and governance practices across Schwab’s expanding alternatives ecosystem.
Build, develop, and retain a high-performing team of investment professionals, portfolio managers, and research talent, strengthening bench depth, decision quality, accountability, and collaboration across an evolving and strategically important platform.
Drive medium- and long-term process improvement initiatives enhancing investment rigor, reporting transparency, regulatory readiness, operational scalability, and confidence among clients, advisors, boards, regulators, and enterprise partners.

What you have

Required Experience

15+ years of progressive senior investment leadership experience across private markets, alternative investments, asset management, portfolio construction, manager research, fund governance, or related investment disciplines.
Deep expertise investing in, allocating to, or overseeing private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, venture capital, secondaries, co-investments, hedge funds, or other alternative investment strategies, with strong judgment across multiple market cycles.
Demonstrated command of private markets portfolio construction, manager due diligence, valuation practices, liquidity management, risk oversight, investment committee governance, and ongoing monitoring of complex, less-liquid investment vehicles.
Proven knowledge of registered fund structures and regulatory requirements, including 1940 Act funds, interval funds, tender-offer funds, business development companies, registered alternatives, and other vehicles designed to broaden access to private market strategies.
Track record leading the development, approval, launch, and commercialization of new investment products, coordinating investment, legal, compliance, operations, finance, product, technology, distribution, and client-facing stakeholders through complex execution milestones.
Experience engaging with boards, regulators, senior executives, risk committees, investment committees, and external partners on investment strategy, governance, valuation, liquidity, risk controls, regulatory readiness, and client impact.
Strong understanding of the operational, legal, compliance, tax, reporting, and technology considerations required to support private assets and alternative investments at scale in a highly regulated financial services environment.
Proven people leadership capability, including the ability to recruit and develop investment talent, set clear expectations, build succession depth, strengthen team operating discipline, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, sound judgment, and continuous improvement.

Key Experiences & Ideal Profile

The ideal candidate is a seasoned private markets and alternative investments leader with the investment credibility, enterprise judgment, and executive presence to scale a strategically important platform within a complex, highly regulated financial services firm. This individual brings both strategic vision and practical execution discipline, with a demonstrated ability to set direction, lead through ambiguity, build durable governance, and translate sophisticated investment concepts into clear decisions for executives, boards, regulators, advisors, and clients.

Key leadership attributes include sound judgment, high integrity, intellectual rigor, executive presence, strong organizational discipline, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders through credibility, clarity, and trust. The leader must be comfortable operating at the intersection of investment management, product innovation, risk governance, legal and regulatory requirements, operations, distribution, and enterprise strategy while creating alignment across teams with different priorities and accountabilities.

Strategic, client-focused leader who can shape Schwab’s point of view on private assets and alternatives while maintaining disciplined stewardship, transparency, and risk management consistent with Schwab’s values.
Credible investment professional with deep private markets expertise and the ability to evaluate opportunities, risks, managers, structures, valuations, liquidity considerations, and portfolio implications with rigor and independence.
Collaborative enterprise leader who builds trusted relationships across SAM/CSIM, Schwab Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, Technology, Forge Global Advisors, SIPSS, external managers, regulators, and board-level stakeholders.
An inclusive people leader who can elevate a specialized team, develop future leaders, reinforce accountability, and create a culture that combines intellectual rigor, prudent risk-taking, operational excellence, high engagement, and continuous learning.
Decisive and balanced executive who can make sound calls amid incomplete information, competing priorities, market uncertainty, regulatory complexity, and evolving client needs while maintaining appropriate escalation, transparency, and governance discipline.
Change leader who can bring structure to ambiguity, mobilize cross-functional teams, build confidence in new investment capabilities, and guide the organization through the operational, cultural, and governance changes required to scale private assets responsibly.
Cisciplined operator who can establish scalable processes, governance routines, reporting frameworks, issue escalation protocols, and decision forums to support growth in a complex and evolving investment category.
An executive communicator who can simplify complexity, provide balanced recommendations, and represent the platform with confidence in senior leadership meetings, committee settings, board discussions, regulatory interactions, and industry forums.

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time for vacation, volunteering, and 28-day sabbatical after every 5 years of service for eligible positions
Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement

jobs.description:
Executive Director

Friends for Sight

Location:
Salt Lake City, Utah (Hybrid)
Friends for Sight offers a flexible hybrid work environment. 
Reports To:
Board of Directors
Status:
Full-Time, Exempt
Compensation:
$84,000–$104,000 annually, depending on experience.

About Friends for Sight

Friends for Sight believes accessible vision care opens the door to discovery—creating a ripple effect for generations. Through vision screenings, comprehensive eye exams, prescription glasses, mobile clinics, and community partnerships, Friends for Sight ensures that every Utahn, regardless of income or background, has access to quality vision care.

Our Vision:
A future where every Utahn has access to the vision care they need to learn, work, and thrive.

Position Summary

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of Friends for Sight and is responsible for advancing the organization's mission through strategic leadership, financial stewardship, fundraising, organizational management, and community engagement. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director leads the organization's staff, cultivates strong partnerships, and ensures Friends for Sight remains financially sustainable while expanding its impact across Utah.

The Executive Director works collaboratively with the Operations Manager and Development Director to implement the Board's strategic vision, strengthen organizational capacity, and build meaningful relationships with donors, volunteers, community partners, and policymakers. 

Essential Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Execute the Board-approved Strategic Plan by providing organizational leadership, accountability, and direction.
Translate strategic priorities into annual organizational goals and measurable objectives.
Lead the leadership team in implementing strategic initiatives and organizational priorities.
Monitor organizational performance, identify emerging opportunities and challenges, and recommend strategic adjustments as needed.
Provide regular updates to the Board of Directors regarding strategic progress, organizational performance, and future priorities.

Organizational Leadership

Recruit, supervise, mentor, and develop high-performing staff.
Cultivate a workplace culture where every employee, volunteer, Board member, partner, and community member is treated with dignity, respect, and fairness, establishing these principles as the standard for all organizational relationships.
Align staff with organizational priorities while fostering collaboration, accountability, transparency, and professional growth.
Promote effective communication and shared leadership across the organization.

Board Relations

Serve as the primary liaison between the Board of Directors and staff.
Support Board recruitment, orientation, engagement, and governance.
Prepare Board meeting materials, strategic recommendations, and organizational reports.
Partner with Board committees to accomplish organizational priorities.
Ensure compliance with Board policies and nonprofit governance best practices.

Financial Stewardship

Partner with accounting staff and the Board Treasurer to develop and oversee the annual operating and program budgets.
Ensure sound financial management, internal controls, and responsible stewardship of organizational resources.
Monitor financial performance and recommend adjustments to support long-term sustainability.
Oversee investment and cash management strategies in collaboration with the Finance Committee.
Ensure compliance with nonprofit accounting standards, grant agreements, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements.
Present accurate and timely financial information to the Board of Directors.

Fundraising & Development

Working closely with the Development Director, the Executive Director will:
Serve as the organization's chief fundraiser and ambassador.
Cultivate relationships with individual donors, foundations, corporations, and government partners.
Identify and pursue new funding opportunities.
Support grant development, stewardship, and donor engagement.
Participate in fundraising campaigns, special events, and donor cultivation activities.
Strengthen long-term philanthropic investment in Friends for Sight.

Community Partnerships & External Relations

Serve as the primary public representative and spokesperson for Friends for Sight.
Develop and strengthen strategic partnerships with healthcare providers, school districts, government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and community leaders.
Represent Friends for Sight at community events, conferences, legislative meetings, and public forums.
Advocate for vision screening and accessible vision care throughout Utah.
Increase the organization's visibility, influence, and reputation statewide.

Program & Operations Leadership

Provide strategic leadership and support to the Operations Manager to ensure programs and operations advance the organization's mission and strategic priorities.
Ensure organizational resources, staffing, and systems support effective program delivery and long-term sustainability.
Review organizational performance and use program data to inform strategic decisions and continuous improvement.
Encourage innovation and organizational learning to strengthen services and expand community impact.

Operations & Compliance

Oversee organizational policies, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
Ensure compliance with HIPAA, employment law, nonprofit regulations, and organizational policies.
Oversee organizational technology, facilities, insurance, and key vendor relationships.
Ensure operational systems support organizational effectiveness and long-term sustainability.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, business administration, public administration, healthcare administration, social work, or a related field.
Minimum of five years of progressively responsible nonprofit leadership experience.
Demonstrated success supervising staff and leading organizational operations.
Experience developing and managing organizational budgets.
Proven success in fundraising, donor cultivation, grant management, and community engagement.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to build collaborative relationships with diverse stakeholders.

Preferred

Master's degree in nonprofit management, business administration, public administration, social work, or a related field.
Executive Director or senior nonprofit leadership experience.
Experience working closely with nonprofit Boards of Directors.
Experience leading organizational growth, strategic planning, and change management.
Familiarity with nonprofit financial management.

Compensation & Benefits

Friends for Sight offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including:
Employer-paid health insurance for the employee
Paid time off and paid holidays
SIMPLE IRA retirement plan with a 3% employer match (fully vested on day 1)
Professional development opportunities, leadership coaching, and continuing education
A flexible, family-friendly hybrid work environment that supports work-life balance

Our Values

At Friends for Sight, we are guided by five core values:

Person-Centered Care

We treat everyone with dignity and respect, valuing each person’s unique needs and experiences.

Mission-Driven Integrity

We are unwavering in our commitment to our mission, making thoughtful, strategic decisions that maximize impact

Community Partnership

We believe lasting impact comes from collaboration—working alongside communities to expand access to quality vision care.

Excellence in Vision Care

We are committed to staying current with vision care best practices, ensuring the delivery of high-quality, accessible services that meet the evolving needs of the communities we serve.

Chief Executive Officer, Habitat for Humanity of the NC Sandhills

Habitat for Humanity of the NC Sandhills is a large, rural affiliate in three counties dedicated to fostering strength, stability, and self-reliance through affordable housing solutions. For 38 years of proven results, we have served more than 1,000 families by building 340+ homes, completing 300+ critical home repairs throughout the Sandhills. In 2022, the affiliate purchased 103-acres projected to provide up to 150 new homes over the next decade. Habitat for Humanity of the NC Sandhills is rooted in Moore County—home to Pinehurst, Southern Pines, and Aberdeen—where a nationally renowned golf legacy creates a unique opportunity to unite the community around affordable housing.
Position Summary

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is responsible for the strategic direction, financial sustainability, and community partnerships of the affiliate. Reporting to and partnering with the Board of Directors, the CEO translates long-term strategic plans into annual operating goals. This executive leader oversees organization-wide alignment across construction, repair programs, family services, fundraising, and ReStore retail operations.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Execution

Translate long-term strategic plans into measurable annual operating plans and KPI dashboards.
Ensure full compliance with Habitat for Humanity International standards, local policies, and legal regulations.
Align operations across fundraising, family services, and ReStore locations.

Financial Leadership & Resource Development

Manage a multi-million-dollar budget with diverse revenue streams (grants, donations, mortgages, and retail).
Drive fundraising strategies, expanding philanthropic support from major donors, corporate sponsors, and grants.
Oversee strict financial controls, forecasting, and scenario planning.

Team Leadership & Organizational Culture

Lead, mentor, and recruit a high-performing, geographically distributed senior leadership team.
Foster an organizational culture rooted in accountability, safety, collaboration, and mission alignment.
Implement clear performance management systems tied directly to strategic goals.

Operations & Rural Program Management

Oversee all multi-county operations, including home construction, repair programs, and volunteer engagement.
Standardize processes to maximize efficiency across all dispersed project sites.
Supervise ReStore retail operations to maximize profitability and mission integration.

Community & Stakeholder Relations

Serve as the primary external ambassador and housing advocate across the rural service area.
Build partnerships with local governments, financial lenders, contractors, and community organizations.
Expand volunteer engagement networks, including corporate and faith-based groups.

Board Governance & Engagement

Act as the primary liaison to the Board of Directors, supplying regular KPI dashboards and performance reports.
Support the Board in fiduciary oversight, policy development, and rural-focused recruitment.

Qualifications

Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Nonprofit Administration, or a related field (or equivalent work experience).
Experience:
Minimum 5 years of executive leadership experience in a nonprofit organization or relevant management role.
Relations:
Proven track record of building local community, governmental, and stakeholder partnerships.
Fundraising:
Direct experience developing targeted fundraising campaigns and cultivating major donors or corporate sponsors is highly preferred.
Communication:
Exceptional verbal, written, and public presentation skills.

About the community

Habitat for Humanity of NC Sandhills is centrally located in North Carolina known for its world-class golf, equestrian activities, outstanding schools, scenic beauty, excellent healthcare and low crime rates. The peaceful environment and strong sense of community make it an ideal place to live. Families and individuals are drawn to easy access to major cities such as Raleigh and Charlotte with the coast just 2 hours away and Blue Ridge Mountains are a scenic 3-hour drive west.

Interested candidates should forward resume and cover letter to ceosearch@sandhillshabitat.org.

jobs.description:
How to Apply

A cover letter and resume are required for consideration for this position. The cover letter should be included in the same document as your resume and should specifically address your interest in this position and highlight related skills and experience.

The Ford School is committed to providing a positive and inclusive work environment. This includes providing employees with flexible work opportunities. You will generally be expected to work in the office 2-3 days per week, after an introductory training period.

Job Summary

The Science, Technology, and Public Policy program at the Gerald R. Ford School of Public Policy is looking for a Managing Director to join our research center. The Managing Director is responsible for day-to-day operations of the STPP program, participating in and providing support for research activities, supervising educational programs, overseeing partnerships, and participating in strategic planning. You will report to the STPP Faculty Director.

Established in 2006, the STPP Program is a research center at the Ford School of Public Policy that is dedicated to advancing the public interest, and specifically social equity and justice, in the development and governance of science and technology through education, research, and community and policy engagement. Our highly interdisciplinary work addresses the ethical, political, social, environmental, health, and equity dimensions of science, technology, and related public policies. This includes a vibrant Community Partnerships Initiative that supports civil society in contributing to public and policy discussions related to science and technology policies, the Technology Assessment Project that analyzes emerging technologies and their implications by drawing lessons from historical analogs, the MiST fellowship that places experts in Michigan state government, a graduate certificate program, and undergraduate programming, among other activities. Our 74 faculty affiliates come from across UM's schools and colleges. We continue to expand STPP to meet the moment, as science and technology become increasingly central to people's daily lives around the world.

Responsibilities*

Administrative Management (20%)

Oversee budgets, staffing, and forecasts; monitor expenditures and ensure alignment with program goals.
Manage multiple grant award programs.
Draft grant proposals and reports as needed.
Identify funding opportunities and recommend program ideas aligned with potential sources.

Team Management (30%)

Manage, direct, and coach team of 4 regular staff and 6-10 student staff to support professional development and center goals.
Lead team meetings and internal activities
Foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment.

Communications (20%)

Develop and implement a communication strategy and marketing efforts aimed at increasing the visibility of the center, including overseeing and/or creating written materials including newsletters, policy briefs, and website/social media content.
Coordinate STPP communications and marketing efforts with communications teams at the Ford School and the University of Michigan
Along with the Faculty Director, represent STPP at public functions, events, workshops, academic conferences, and policy events to publicize the organization's activities and garner new opportunities.

Partnerships (30%)

Along with the Community Partnerships Coordinator, the MiST Project Manager, and the Faculty Director, identify, develop, and cultivate new and existing partnerships with people and organizations outside of the University.
Establish and maintain good working relationships and collaborative agreements with elected/appointed leaders, policy makers, community groups, funders, and other entities.
Liaise with other units and departments within the Ford School, at U-M, and external to the university.

Graduate-level degree in public policy, science, engineering, humanities, or social sciences
5+ years managing complex programs including a research component
3+ years in a leadership role, including managing staff
Experience managing outreach activities and strong communication and fundraising skills
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
Experience working in a research-intensive environment, including with faculty
Commitment to principles of social justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion. For more information on the University's commitment to these principles, please visit: https://diversity.umich.edu/

Desired Qualifications*

Experience developing and implementing qualitative and/or quantitative research.
Demonstrated interest in at least one area of science and technology policy, broadly defined.
Interest in ethics, equity, and/or justice in science, technology, and environment.

Benefits

In addition to a career filled with purpose and opportunity, The University of Michigan offers a comprehensive benefits package to help you stay well, protect yourself and your family and plan for a secure future. Benefits include:

Generous time off
A retirement plan that provides two-for-one matching contributions with immediate vesting

Dream Job

This is a rare chance to step into a President and CEO role with real latitude to define what comes next for a well-established regional organization. The right person will build direct relationships with investors, government leaders, and business owners across five counties, translating that access into concrete economic wins for the community. It suits a confident, entrepreneurial leader who wants ownership over strategy and execution, not just oversight, and who is ready to make a visible, lasting mark on a region already gaining national attention.

Serve as the primary spokesperson and external face of the organization, representing the region to investors, government officials, business leaders, and the public.

Lead the organization's approach to workforce development and talent attraction, including regional branding and marketing initiatives that support long-term growth.
Guide economic development priorities across the five-county region, including business retention efforts and coordination on site selection, business development, and government relations.
Oversee the organization's financial and operational health, including budgeting, planning, and financial reporting in partnership with internal and contracted support staff.
Engage effectively with the Board of Directors and executive committee, ensuring strong governance and alignment on strategic direction.
Pursue grant funding and public/private funding mechanisms to diversify and strengthen the organization's financial base.
Represent the region at state and regional events, including advocacy efforts with legislators and state officials.
Develop and communicate metrics that demonstrate the organization's impact and the return on investment for stakeholders.
Anticipate change and bring together diverse stakeholders to get ahead of regional challenges before they escalate.

Qualifications

Required

Five or more years of progressively responsible career growth, including at least three years in a leadership capacity, with a demonstrated track record as a catalyst for goal implementation and business growth.
Strong financial acumen and business background sufficient to understand and manage the organization's operating and fiscal plans, and to advocate for local and state support around investment, legislation, policy, and funding.
A collaborative, entrepreneurial mindset with a proven ability to build relationships across diverse stakeholder groups, and the credibility to earn the trust and support of stakeholders with differing priorities.
Familiarity with the Wisconsin economic development landscape. Must reside within the five-county region (Adams, Lincoln, Marathon, Portage, or Wood County).
Knowledge of regional branding, marketing, and talent attraction strategies, with the ability to build and implement workforce development initiatives.

Preferred

Economic development experience, including familiarity with site selection, business development, and government relations, and the ability to align regional resources to capture business growth opportunities.
Grant writing knowledge and experience with public and private funding mechanisms.
Experience with event planning.
Bachelor's degree in business, public policy, economics, or a related field.

Outstanding communicator and relationship builder who engages effectively with a governing board.
Natural connector who anticipates change and brings stakeholders together proactively.

jobs.title: Managing Director & Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments
jobs.description:
Your opportunity

Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments

Overview

The Managing Director & Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments will report to the Chief Executive Officer of Schwab Asset Management and lead a team responsible for managing our expanding portfolio of non-traditional investment management offerings including the planned launch of the Schwab Private Company Fund.

Key Outcomes

This leader will be accountable for establishing the strategic direction, investment governance, operating model, and risk discipline required to scale Schwab’s private assets and alternative investments platform. The role requires sound independent judgment within approved investment guidelines, strong executive presence, and the ability to connect investment strategy, product innovation, risk management, and client outcomes across SAM/CSIM and the broader Schwab enterprise.

Set the long-term strategic agenda for Private Assets and Alternative Investments, including portfolio construction philosophy, product roadmap, governance standards, risk controls, and operating discipline across current and future offerings.
Lead the successful development, launch, and scaling of the Schwab Private Company Fund and related offerings, ensuring investment design, legal structure, compliance oversight, operations, distribution readiness, and client experience are aligned from concept through commercialization.
Make independent investment and business decisions within approved guidelines, balancing growth, liquidity, valuation, manager selection, operational complexity, fiduciary obligations, regulatory expectations, and Schwab’s reputation for client-first stewardship.
Oversee risk across the Private Assets and Alternative Investments platform, partnering closely with Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, and Technology teams to ensure strong controls, clear accountability, scalable processes, and effective issue escalation.
Serve as a senior investment and business advisor to the Chief Executive Officer of SAM/CSIM and the broader executive team, providing informed perspectives on private markets, alternative investment trends, fund performance, competitive dynamics, product opportunities, and enterprise implications.
Represent the platform with credibility before the Funds Board of Directors, SAM/CSIM committees, firm-wide risk committees, regulators, and senior enterprise stakeholders, translating complex investment, liquidity, valuation, and governance topics into clear executive-level recommendations.
Partner with leadership on the construction and oversight of SPVs serving as building blocks for the Schwab Private Company Fund, ensuring close coordination across sourcing, due diligence, structuring, valuation, operational readiness, and ongoing monitoring.
Provide leadership and expertise to third-party investment oversight and asset allocation forums involving private assets, helping shape manager due diligence, allocation recommendations, risk evaluation, and governance practices across Schwab’s expanding alternatives ecosystem.
Build, develop, and retain a high-performing team of investment professionals, portfolio managers, and research talent, strengthening bench depth, decision quality, accountability, and collaboration across an evolving and strategically important platform.
Drive medium- and long-term process improvement initiatives enhancing investment rigor, reporting transparency, regulatory readiness, operational scalability, and confidence among clients, advisors, boards, regulators, and enterprise partners.

What you have

Required Experience

15+ years of progressive senior investment leadership experience across private markets, alternative investments, asset management, portfolio construction, manager research, fund governance, or related investment disciplines.
Deep expertise investing in, allocating to, or overseeing private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, venture capital, secondaries, co-investments, hedge funds, or other alternative investment strategies, with strong judgment across multiple market cycles.
Demonstrated command of private markets portfolio construction, manager due diligence, valuation practices, liquidity management, risk oversight, investment committee governance, and ongoing monitoring of complex, less-liquid investment vehicles.
Proven knowledge of registered fund structures and regulatory requirements, including 1940 Act funds, interval funds, tender-offer funds, business development companies, registered alternatives, and other vehicles designed to broaden access to private market strategies.
Track record leading the development, approval, launch, and commercialization of new investment products, coordinating investment, legal, compliance, operations, finance, product, technology, distribution, and client-facing stakeholders through complex execution milestones.
Experience engaging with boards, regulators, senior executives, risk committees, investment committees, and external partners on investment strategy, governance, valuation, liquidity, risk controls, regulatory readiness, and client impact.
Strong understanding of the operational, legal, compliance, tax, reporting, and technology considerations required to support private assets and alternative investments at scale in a highly regulated financial services environment.
Proven people leadership capability, including the ability to recruit and develop investment talent, set clear expectations, build succession depth, strengthen team operating discipline, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, sound judgment, and continuous improvement.

Key Experiences & Ideal Profile

The ideal candidate is a seasoned private markets and alternative investments leader with the investment credibility, enterprise judgment, and executive presence to scale a strategically important platform within a complex, highly regulated financial services firm. This individual brings both strategic vision and practical execution discipline, with a demonstrated ability to set direction, lead through ambiguity, build durable governance, and translate sophisticated investment concepts into clear decisions for executives, boards, regulators, advisors, and clients.

Key leadership attributes include sound judgment, high integrity, intellectual rigor, executive presence, strong organizational discipline, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders through credibility, clarity, and trust. The leader must be comfortable operating at the intersection of investment management, product innovation, risk governance, legal and regulatory requirements, operations, distribution, and enterprise strategy while creating alignment across teams with different priorities and accountabilities.

Strategic, client-focused leader who can shape Schwab’s point of view on private assets and alternatives while maintaining disciplined stewardship, transparency, and risk management consistent with Schwab’s values.
Credible investment professional with deep private markets expertise and the ability to evaluate opportunities, risks, managers, structures, valuations, liquidity considerations, and portfolio implications with rigor and independence.
Collaborative enterprise leader who builds trusted relationships across SAM/CSIM, Schwab Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, Technology, Forge Global Advisors, SIPSS, external managers, regulators, and board-level stakeholders.
An inclusive people leader who can elevate a specialized team, develop future leaders, reinforce accountability, and create a culture that combines intellectual rigor, prudent risk-taking, operational excellence, high engagement, and continuous learning.
Decisive and balanced executive who can make sound calls amid incomplete information, competing priorities, market uncertainty, regulatory complexity, and evolving client needs while maintaining appropriate escalation, transparency, and governance discipline.
Change leader who can bring structure to ambiguity, mobilize cross-functional teams, build confidence in new investment capabilities, and guide the organization through the operational, cultural, and governance changes required to scale private assets responsibly.
Cisciplined operator who can establish scalable processes, governance routines, reporting frameworks, issue escalation protocols, and decision forums to support growth in a complex and evolving investment category.
An executive communicator who can simplify complexity, provide balanced recommendations, and represent the platform with confidence in senior leadership meetings, committee settings, board discussions, regulatory interactions, and industry forums.

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time for vacation, volunteering, and 28-day sabbatical after every 5 years of service for eligible positions
Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement
Health, dental, and vision insurance

The University of Michigan is establishing a flagship institutional hub in Washington, DC, located in an 11,600-square-foot multi-use facility at 1700 M St NW. Reporting to the Provost's Office and operating in collaboration with its institutional co-sponsors, you will manage logistics, coordinate with property management and remote university partners, and build a reliable network of support resources to ensure consistent facility coverage. This is a term-limited appointment designed to support the launch and early operations of this new institutional hub.

Track space usage, service requests, user feedback, staffing needs, and recurring issues to recommend operational improvements and support long-term planning.
Support launch and activation activities, including move-in logistics, vendor onboarding, workflow testing, and development of a site operations strategy.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience in operations, facilities management, hospitality, business administration, higher education administration, or a related field.
7 years of progressively responsible operations experience, including experience in facilities, events, hospitality, coworking/shared workspace, or another complex public-facing environment.
5 years of experience hiring, training, or directly supervising staff.

Why Work at Michigan?

Lead the identification, development and implementation of the MWR regional strategy for transformative innovation across all Global Practices and M&S functions.
Drive alignment of MWR innovation objectives with overall Corporate, Global Practice and Regional goals, ensuring a strong linkage to business drivers and the MWR vision of success.
Challenge existing processes, methodologies, and mindset to rethink how we do business and execute projects for our clients.
Develop and implement the MWR “Innovation Operating System”, a structured framework that makes innovation an integral element in the functioning of the entire region, repeatable, measurable, and scalable. Position Overview

Irvine Nature Center seeks a strategic, entrepreneurial, and results-oriented Director of Advancement to lead all fundraising, marketing, communications, and revenue-generation efforts for the organization.

As a key member of Irvine’s leadership team, the Director of Advancement will develop and execute an integrated advancement strategy focused on increasing contributed and earned revenue, expanding community engagement, elevating organizational visibility, and strengthening Irvine’s long-term sustainability and impact.

This role oversees all fundraising activities, including major gifts, annual giving, corporate and

foundation partnerships, planned giving, stewardship, special events, and the completion of Irvine’s $10 million capital campaign. The position also leads all marketing and communications efforts with a strong emphasis on dramatically increasing visibility, attendance, and revenue for Irvine’s public programs, events, camps, and educational offerings.

The Director of Advancement will serve as a strategic partner to the Executive and Deputy Directors and help build a modern, high-performing Office of Advancement that aligns fundraising, marketing, communications, and audience development strategies to drive organizational growth.

The Advancement team currently includes three full-time fundraising staff members, with funding available for the successful candidate to evaluate future staffing structure and departmental growth.

The ideal candidate is a highly motivated revenue-builder who combines strategic leadership with hands-on execution and has a proven ability to grow fundraising results, expand audiences, and drive engagement through effective marketing and relationship management.

Key Responsibilities

Advancement Strategy & Revenue Growth

Develop and lead a comprehensive advancement strategy focused on increasing philanthropic and earned revenue.
Partner with the Executive Director and Board of Trustees to establish fundraising priorities, revenue goals, and growth strategies.
Build and strengthen a culture of philanthropy and revenue accountability across the organization.
Track and analyze fundraising, marketing, attendance, and engagement metrics to drive decision-making and performance.
Serve as staff liaison to the board Development Committee and support board engagement in fundraising and donor cultivation.

Fundraising & Philanthropic Partnerships

Lead all fundraising initiatives, including:
Major gifts
Annual giving
Corporate sponsorships and partnerships
Foundation and institutional giving
Planned giving
Campaign fundraising
Special events and donor engagement
Manage a portfolio of major donors and high-capacity prospects.
Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward donors, sponsors, and institutional funders.
Partner closely with the Executive Director and Board on donor strategy and major gift solicitations.
Develop strategies to diversify and grow contributed revenue streams.
Oversee donor stewardship and engagement efforts to strengthen long-term relationships and retention.

Marketing, Communications & Earned Revenue Growth

Lead all marketing and communications efforts with a strong focus on increasing attendance

and revenue for Irvine’s public programs, camps, classes, events, and educational offerings.

Develop and execute integrated marketing campaigns across digital, print, email, social media, advertising, and public relations channels.
Strengthen Irvine’s visibility, brand awareness, and audience engagement throughout the

region.

Oversee organizational communications, including:
Brand management
Website and digital presence
Social media strategy
Email marketing
Advertising and promotions
Media relations
Publications and storytelling
Collaborate with program staff to market programs effectively and maximize participation and earned revenue opportunities.
Monitor marketing analytics and audience data to optimize campaign performance and return on investment.
Ensure consistent, compelling, mission-driven messaging across all platforms.

Capital Campaign Leadership

Support the successful completion of Irvine’s $10 million capital campaign.
Partner with campaign leadership, volunteers, consultants, and board members to maintain campaign momentum and donor engagement.
Oversee campaign communications, stewardship, and donor strategy.

Team Leadership & Advancement Operations

Lead, supervise, mentor, and grow the Advancement team.
Evaluate departmental structure, workflows, systems, and staffing needs to support organizational growth.
Build a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing advancement culture focused on results.
Oversee advancement operations, donor systems, reporting, and data integrity.
Partner with Finance to ensure accurate gift processing, reconciliation, and reporting.
Develop and manage departmental budgets, forecasts, and revenue projections.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience in fundraising, marketing,

communications, nonprofit management, business administration, or related field.

Minimum of 8 years of progressive leadership experience in advancement, fundraising, marketing, communications, or related fields.
Demonstrated success growing fundraising revenue and securing major gifts.
Proven experience developing marketing strategies that increase audience engagement, participation, and revenue.
Strong understanding of integrated fundraising, marketing, and communications strategy.
Exceptional relationship-building and interpersonal skills.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
Strong strategic thinking, organizational leadership, and project management abilities.
Experience supervising staff and building collaborative teams.
Ability to analyze data and use metrics to drive strategy and performance.
High degree of professionalism, initiative, discretion, and sound judgment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in environmental, educational, cultural, or mission-driven nonprofit organizations.
Experience leading or supporting a capital campaign.
Knowledge of CRM and fundraising systems such as Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge NXT or similar

platforms.

Experience with digital marketing, audience development, and revenue-generating campaigns.
Interest in environmental education, conservation, nature-based learning, or community engagement.

Physical Requirements

Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds occasionally.
Ability to attend events, donor meetings, and organizational activities onsite and offsite.
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

To Apply

Please submit a resume, cover letter, and three professional references to HR@ExploreNature.org.

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check and fingerprinting process.
